To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of metaphors by patients and their relatives is a very common and important part of their communication with the health care staff, that the metaphors used in this communication are often related to the patients' experiences of their illness and its treatment, and that the metaphors are also often related to the patient's experience of his or her life situation in general.

the use of metaphors in our mouths is a very important part of the way we talk about our patients, that metaphors are used to describe the patients' experiences, and that metaphors are also used to describe the way the patient is treated.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how metaphors can be used to create new knowledge about the world, and in this paper we focus on the use of metaphors as a means of understanding the nature and role of metaphors in psychiatric practice.
the role of metaphor in the construction of psychiatric discourse.
the role of the metaphor in the process of communication between patients and doctors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence does not support the use of antipsychotics in the treatment of schizophrenia.
the evidence is insufficient to determine if a relationship exists between the use of psychotropic medications and the development of tardive dyskinesia.

there is no evidence that the use of the terms'schizophrenia' and'schizoaffective disorder' are helpful to patients, or that they have any validity in terms of the underlying pathophysiology of these conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to show that the patients’ experiences of the treatment process are important for the treatment outcome.
we have been able to show that the language of the patient is a very important part of the therapeutic process.
we found that the patients' experiences with the psychiatric services were characterized by the use of metaphors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way that we speak about mental illness matters.
the way we speak about the patient and his/her illness is important and that the way we think and speak about the patient's illness can be changed.
the language of psychiatry is not neutral.
